situation: A job scheduler keeps a priority queue of tasks. When a task's priority is updated, it should bubble up or down in the heap, but the update operation only changes the stored priority without re-heapifying. Under load, high-priority tasks end up stuck behind low-priority ones.
deadEnds: Tried sorting the entire queue on every update, which fixed correctness but tanked performance
Suspected the comparator was inverted (min-heap vs max-heap), but that was correct
Added logging and saw the priority field was updated — assumed the heap was fine
unlock: Mutating a node's priority without restoring the heap invariant leaves the structure inconsistent. After updating the value, calling siftUp or siftDown on the affected index restored correct ordering.
